_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401909994.text: Orlando arrive with some momentum under new coach Sean Sweeney, who replaced the fired Jamahl Mosley: after a stretch where the mood was described as 'it's not working', the Magic have won three straight, though Paolo Banchero is still out with a high ankle sprain. Boston are flying, six straight wins and Jayson Tatum talking up 'a really, really good team', but this is the second night of a back-to-back after a 37-point rout of Dallas. The news angle leans a little towards Orlando keeping it closer than the records suggest.

401909995.text: Donovan Mitchell was taken off Cleveland's injury report after resting a bruised knee, so the Cavaliers should have their star back even with Evan Mobley out again. Cleveland are also coming off a chaotic trip, stuck overnight in Miami by an FAA ground stop before beating Dallas with all five starters resting. Chicago have won two straight but lost Caleb Wilson to hand surgery, and Nic Claxton is already being floated as a trade candidate. On balance the news leans towards Cleveland.

401909996.text: Washington look rattled: after a 147-119 loss to Houston, their seventh in a row, Brian Keefe called it 'not a commitment to defense', demanded accountability and cut his press conference to about three minutes. Trae Young went scoreless for the first time in his career and questions about his future are growing. Memphis are 9-4 but banged up, with several frontcourt players questionable. The mental angle leans towards Memphis.

401909997.text: Philadelphia are on the second night of a back-to-back, and neither Joel Embiid (plantar fascia) nor LeBron James has played both ends of one this season, so a thinned-out 76ers lineup is possible. Brooklyn have their own noise: Jordi Fernandez's rotation is being questioned after a heavy loss to Memphis, and Michael Porter Jr. is expected back after missing Saturday for personal reasons. If Philadelphia rest their stars, the news angle leans towards Brooklyn keeping it closer.

401909998.text: Both teams arrive on four-game winning streaks, and Miami's own preview calls Houston their 'toughest test to date'. Fred VanVleet is back from the torn ACL that cost him last season and says he is 'appreciating every minute', but the Rockets are coming off a game in Washington the night before. No locker-room or trade storylines were found; the angle is fairly neutral, with a slight lean to the rested home side.

401909999.text: Portland coach Micah Nori returns to Minnesota, where he spent five seasons as Chris Finch's top assistant, so he knows this opponent well. The Timberwolves come in stung: Finch called Saturday's home loss to Chicago an 'unacceptable performance', and they are still without Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo, though they had won five of six without Edwards. Expect a sharp, motivated Minnesota response; the angle leans slightly to the home side.

401910003.text: This is the second game of a two-night set in Minneapolis, so both teams know each other inside out and the loser of Monday's game gets an instant revenge spot. Micah Nori, Finch's former top assistant, is facing his old staff twice in two nights, while Minnesota are still without Anthony Edwards. Portland are also still waiting on Ja Morant's return from a hamstring strain. Read Monday's result first; the angle tilts towards whichever side lost it.

401910000.text: New Orleans are in turmoil: Dejounte Murray requested a trade through Klutch Sports, posted (and partly deleted) 'THE SABOTAGE IS REAL', and the club has confirmed it will explore deals, all during a six-game losing streak that included a 51-point loss to Golden State. The Warriors are without Stephen Curry (torn oblique) but have found sparks, and New Orleans native LJ Cryer gets a homecoming game. The news angle leans clearly towards Golden State.

401910001.text: Phoenix come in on the second night of a back-to-back after trailing the Lakers by 31, with their starting five now -44 together and calls growing for a lineup change; they are also winless on the road and are linked to Dejounte Murray in trade talk. Denver are 6-0 against losing teams, the kind of opponent they have handled. The mental angle leans towards Denver.

401910002.text: A quick rematch: the Knicks won in overtime in Toronto on Sunday, their 14th straight win over the Raptors, after Toronto blew a 13-point fourth-quarter lead to drop a fourth straight. Darko Rajakovic blamed a loss of discipline, but Scottie Barnes' 30-point return is a lift, and RJ Barrett (contract year) and Immanuel Quickley face their former team again. Kawhi Leonard remains out. Revenge motivation leans slightly towards Toronto, though the Knicks own this matchup lately.

401910004.text: San Antonio have won 12 straight and just beat Utah without De'Aaron Fox (hip tightness), with Dylan Harper scoring 31 as the young guards absorbed the ball-handling. Detroit arrive after a 137-117 loss in Miami, with J.B. Bickerstaff saying the defense 'hasn't been to standard, and that's on me' and Jalen Duren still out. The news angle leans towards San Antonio.

401910006.text: Utah have lost 12 straight and are badly depleted, with Lauri Markkanen (hand), Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic all out; Mo Bamba admitted the frustration but said the locker room does not feel hopeless. The Clippers have their first two-game win streak of the season but still no timeline for Bradley Beal. The angle leans towards the Clippers, with rookie Darryn Peterson the main Utah wildcard.

401910005.text: The Lakers open a four-game homestand on an eight-game win streak, and Austin Reaves (heel bruise) may play depending on 'pain tolerance', per JJ Redick. Charlotte look like a team in a funk since the LaMelo Ball trade, having lost 8 of 9, and Coby White asked 'how do we stop the bleeding?' with Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder hurt. The news angle leans towards the Lakers.
